target.title: feat(review): classify unrecoverable UX bugs as P0
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

ClawSweeper's technical-severity rubric can under-rank a user-experience failure that stops a non-technical first-time or community user from completing download, install, update, setup, onboarding, auth/provider setup, a first useful run, or in-product recovery.

This PR makes a genuinely blocked product path a release-blocker signal:

- `triagePriority: "P0"`
- `impact:ux-release-blocker`

It also adds `impact:ux-friction` for support-heavy or confusing flows where the user can still proceed.

Closes #386. Related context: openclaw/openclaw#75947 and openclaw/openclaw#99141.

## Why This Change Was Made

Implementation difficulty is not the same as user impact. A missing affordance can be technically small and still end a new user's journey when the only recovery path is terminal commands, config edits, log inspection, manual file edits, internal knowledge, or maintainer support.

The override is deliberately narrow: the user-facing path must be blocked. Ordinary advanced configuration and optional power-user workflows do not become P0 merely because they use a terminal or config file.

The implementation reuses the existing priority and impact-label plumbing rather than adding a new decision field. It updates the prompt, JSON schema, managed label definitions, triage-dashboard grouping, documentation, and focused tests together.

## User Impact

After deployment, qualifying issues are visible as P0 UX release blockers. Recoverable friction remains P1/P2. Pull requests still receive no issue-only impact labels.

This is triage/rubric work. It does not claim to fix the underlying OpenClaw UI or replace the product work tracked in openclaw/openclaw#75947.

## Evidence

- Rebased on current ClawSweeper `main` at `a397ae06d380c715dc2721e45ae682fb6e41b4b8`.
- `pnpm run build:all` passed.
- Focused dashboard/parser/label-policy proof passed: 93 tests, 0 failures.
- Real local-only review against fresh OpenClaw `main` (`9d68f877ac3ea28c1abffaf7a043c8c916bea217`) and openclaw/openclaw#98674 produced a high-confidence `keep_open`, `P0`, and only `impact:ux-release-blocker`; it found the issue source-reproducible and removed an unsupported maturity label.
- Structured autoreview of the policy tightening: no actionable findings, confidence 0.86.
- Structured autoreview of the complete branch: no actionable findings, confidence 0.83.
- Full local `pnpm run check` and exact-head GitHub CI are running on `db45fb0a4c7ca61c4d63871d993645189c13a1ce`; final proof will be posted before merge.

Real replay command shape:

```text
pnpm run review -- --local-only --target-repo openclaw/openclaw --item-number 98674 --target-dir <fresh-openclaw-main> --artifact-dir <temporary-artifact-dir> --codex-timeout-ms 600000 --verbose
```
